pass.answer: The two sources point at different bottlenecks. Source A ran the queue for six hours and saw SSD throughput hold until the log grew to about 40 GB, then lose two thirds of its rate in minutes; the authors call this the "write amplification cliff" and saw it on every SSD they tried. Source B looked at containers that start and stop often: each spent about nine seconds rebuilding its index before taking traffic, and across a day of scaling up and down that "cold-start tax" ate more capacity than any steady-state limit did. For a long-running deployment A matters more; for bursty autoscaling B does.
pass.why: own words throughout, coined terms quoted
